question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for freedom to manage religious affairs?
solution:
The correct answer is, '**Article 26**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 26 states **public order rights, morality and health, and religious denomination**.

 
 
• to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes;
 
• to manage its affairs in matters of religion;
 
• to own and acquire movable and immovable property; and
 
• to administer such property by the law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 35** states that **the parliament (not the state) will have the power to make laws in certain specified conditions**.

 
 
• It also provides **power to the parliament to prescribe punishments for offenses of fundamental rights.**
 
• Article 35A empowers **Jammu and Kashmir permanent residents with the privileges** of acquisition of property, public sector jobs, etc. 
 
 
 
• **Article 12** **defines the term 'the State**' that has been heavily used in the Constitution of India.
 
 
• It includes the Government and Parliament of India, the government and legislature of every state and local authority, and other authorities in the territory of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 49 obligates the State to protect every monument**, place, and object of historical significance from destruction, removal, disfiguration, and spoilation.
